stem: The earliest evidence of animal Husbandry and agriculture in India has come from:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The earliest evidence of animal husbandry and agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been found at Mehrgarh (present-day Pakistan). On the basis of the latest discoveries, the earliest site with evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent is Lahuradewa, located in Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Evidence of rice has been found here dating to the period between about 8000 BCE and 7000 BCE. It is noteworthy that before this latest discovery, Mehrgarh was considered the earliest agricultural site in the Indian subcontinent, where evidence of wheat has been found, while Koldihwa (on the bank of the Belan River, Prayagraj district) is considered the site with the earliest evidence of rice.

stem: Which one of the following periods is also known as the Chalcolithic Age?
expl: The Copper–Stone Age is also called the Chalcolithic period. Cultures in which stone tools are found in use along with copper tools are generally called Chalcolithic cultures.

stem: Which river valley in India was the first human fossil obtained from?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In India, the first evidence of a human fossil was found at the archaeological site of Hathnora (Sehore, Madhya Pradesh), located in the Narmada Valley. It was discovered in 1982 by Arun Sonakia, a palaeontologist of the Geological Survey of India.

stem: Which of the following states is the Bhimbetka site located in?
expl: The Bhimbetka archaeological site remained a centre of human activities from the Early Stone Age to the historical period. It is located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. Hundreds of examples of prehistoric paintings have been found in the caves of Bhimbetka. The main themes of the rock paintings include collective dance, outlined human figures, hunting, animals and birds, war, and daily activities of ancient human life. So far, about 750 rock shelters have been identified here, and paintings have been found in about 500 of them.
